note.en: What you see: Turned leftward in the mid oesophagus, the sector cuts the descending thoracic aorta in cross section as a bright round ring with pulsatile walls. The pleural line and lung sit beside it and the spine shadow anchors the far side. Withdrawing slowly from diaphragm to arch walks the ring along the whole thoracic course, so a flap line, clot crescent or wall haematoma can be traced along its length.

steps.en: What you see: Turned leftward in the mid oesophagus, the sector cuts the descending thoracic aorta in cross section as a bright round ring with pulsatile walls. The pleural line and lung sit beside it and the spine shadow anchors the far side. Withdrawing slowly from diaphragm to arch walks the ring along the whole thoracic course, so a flap line, clot crescent or wall haematoma can be traced along its length.
Landmarks to confirm: Descending aorta in cross section, pleural line, lung edge, thoracic spine shadow, oesophageal wall layers beside the vessel.

Common mistakes and correction: Mistaking the azygos arch for a dissection flap: confirm any line in two planes before reporting. Calling pleural fluid a second lumen: fluid lies outside the bright wall, so trace the wall fully around the ring. Letting oesophageal wall layers mimic clot: centre the vessel and confirm the layers move with swallowing.

Normal values with units: Probe station from about 30 cm withdrawing toward 25 cm from the incisors. Multiplane angle 0 degrees. In health the ring is single channelled with a thin bright wall that expands in systole. Any mobile flap line across the lumen with flow in two channels suggests dissection and needs immediate senior review.

Pitfalls: Mirror artefact in the adjacent lung can fake a second vessel, so confirm every finding while withdrawing along the course. In suspected dissection record the full length from diaphragm to arch rather than one frozen ring. Severe atheroma throws shadows that hide the far wall, so lower gain and sweep before judging.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: From the mid oesophageal station at about 30 cm, turn the probe leftward toward the descending aorta with the multiplane at 0 degrees. Centre the round aortic ring and withdraw slowly from the diaphragm toward the arch, watching the ring travel along its course. Keep the depth shallow since the vessel lies close to the probe. If the ring turns oval, the cut has gone oblique, so straighten the probe and re centre before judging.

q.en: How is the descending aorta short axis obtained?

o.en: Rightward toward the superior vena cava
Leftward toward the descending aorta at 0 degrees
Deep into the stomach with flexion

why.en: A leftward turn at 0 degrees in the mid oesophagus brings the descending aorta into cross section.

q.en: A line crosses the aortic ring. What is correct?

o.en: Freeze one ring and report dissection
Trace any line along the course and confirm in two planes before reporting

why.en: Mimics are common, so trace the line along the vessel and confirm in two planes before reporting dissection.

q.en: The ring turns oval and the wall looks doubled. What first?

o.en: Straighten the probe and re centre the ring

why.en: An oval ring means an oblique cut, so straighten and re centre before judging the wall.
